sheets.title: Level 0 — Application & Commitment
sheets.intro: The vendor/developer formally applies and commits to the process. All items are documents. Critical items (red) must all be Met.

criteria.title: Letter of application to have the EMR system tested for use in the HIE, signed by the vendor's/developer's authorized signatory
criteria.evidence: Signed letter of application + proof of authority
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit a letter of application on official letterhead, signed by an authorized signatory, with proof of authority (secretary's certificate / board resolution; office order for in-house systems).

Purpose: The vendor or developer formally asks to be evaluated.
criteria.validator_guide: Check the letter is on official letterhead, dated, and signed by an authorized signatory (with proof of authority, e.g. secretary's certificate or office order for in-house systems).

criteria.title: Vendor/developer contact persons designated: (1) product/technical lead, (2) integration (FHIR) developer, (3) data privacy contact
criteria.evidence: Designation / contact list
criteria.developer_guide:
Name three contact persons — product/technical lead, FHIR integration developer, data privacy contact — with position, email and mobile number.

Purpose: The DOH knows who is accountable for the product, the integration and privacy questions during testing.
criteria.validator_guide:
Count the roles with a named person, position and contact details in the letter or designation.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.

sub_items.text: Product / technical lead named (position, email, mobile)
Data privacy contact named (position, email, mobile)

criteria.title: EMR system identified: product name, version/build under test, deployment model, facility types it is offered for
criteria.evidence: Completed System Profile
criteria.developer_guide:
Complete the System Profile Sheet: product name, exact version/build to be tested, deployment model, and facility types the system is offered for.

Purpose: We know exactly which system and version is being tested; results apply to that version only.
criteria.validator_guide: Check System Profile A.1–A.7 and B.1–B.2 are complete and match the letter.

criteria.title: Signed undertaking to conform to the PH Core and PHeReF IGs, to be re-tested on IG version change or major system release, and to use only test data on the sandbox
criteria.evidence: Signed undertaking
criteria.developer_guide:
Sign the undertaking to (1) conform to PH Core and PHeReF, (2) request re-testing on IG version change or major release, and (3) use only test data on the sandbox.

Purpose: Because the IGs are drafts, the vendor agrees to keep up with updates; no real patient data is used in testing.
criteria.validator_guide: Check the signed undertaking names both IGs, the re-test clause and the test-data-only clause.

criteria.title: Contact persons (from L0-02) attended the initial coordination meeting with the Regional Validation Team (in person or virtual)
criteria.evidence: Attendance sheet or minutes of the coordination meeting
criteria.developer_guide:
Ensure the three contact persons attend the initial coordination meeting with the Regional Validation Team (in person or virtual) to agree on the process and schedule.

Purpose: The vendor understands the process and the schedule before testing begins.
criteria.validator_guide:
Count the contact persons in the attendance / minutes of the coordination meeting.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.

sub_items.text: Product / technical lead attended the coordination meeting
Integration (FHIR) developer attended the coordination meeting
Data privacy contact attended the coordination meeting

criteria.title: Access to the test (sandbox) endpoint requested and granted
criteria.evidence: Access confirmation
criteria.developer_guide:
Request sandbox (test endpoint) access from the Regional Validation Team and confirm a successful connection.

Purpose: The vendor can connect to the test servers.
criteria.validator_guide: Check the confirmation email / access log from the endpoint administrator.

sheets.title: Level 1 — Product Documentation
sheets.intro: Documentation of the EMR system itself. Facility-level legal, privacy, infrastructure and personnel requirements are outside the scope of this tool.

criteria.title: Process flows of the eReferral module as implemented in the system, for ALL three: (a) referring, (b) receiving, (c) back-referral
criteria.evidence: Process flow diagrams
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit process flow diagrams of the eReferral module for referring, receiving and back-referral, showing the actual system screens and steps.

Purpose: Shows how the system moves a referral step by step. All three are required (all-or-nothing, per DOH draft).
criteria.validator_guide: Check that diagrams exist for all three flows and show the system screens/steps. If any one is missing, mark Not Met.

criteria.title: User manual of the eReferral module contains ALL seven required sections (all-or-nothing): (1) system overview & user roles, (2) referring workflow step-by-step, (3) receiving workflow step-by-step, (4) back-referral workflow, (5) downtime/offline behaviour, (6) troubleshooting & error messages, (7) vendor support contacts & escalation
criteria.evidence: User manual
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit the eReferral module user manual with a table of contents covering ALL 7 required sections, including how users check the server status and what the system does during downtime or offline operation. Titles, order and format (printed, PDF or online help) are the vendor's choice — only the content is checked.

Purpose: Checks the CONTENT of the manual once, at product level. All seven sections are required: a manual missing any one section scores 0% (all-or-nothing).
criteria.validator_guide:
Check the table of contents and the body of the manual for each of the 7 sections. Mark each sub-item (↳) below so missing sections are listed.
All-or-nothing: the criterion scores 100% only if ALL 7 sub-items are Met; if any one is Not Met the score is 0%.

sub_items.text: Server status check & downtime / offline behaviour

criteria.title: Supported FHIR interactions documented per resource (which resources are created, read, updated, searched), e.g. a CapabilityStatement (Connectathon Issue #3)
criteria.evidence: CapabilityStatement or equivalent document
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit a CapabilityStatement (or equivalent) listing each FHIR resource used, its supported interactions (POST, PUT, GET, search) and search parameters.

Purpose: Removes ambiguity about what the system actually sends and receives.
criteria.validator_guide: Check the document lists each resource used in TS1/TS2 with its interactions (POST/PUT/GET/search).

criteria.evidence: System architecture diagram (high-level is sufficient) + demonstration
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit a system architecture diagram showing the EMR, the eReferral function (built-in or a separate system) and how patient details flow from the EMR record into the referral. A high-level diagram is sufficient — internal component, network or infrastructure details are not required. Any integration method is acceptable (shared database, API, FHIR, HL7 v2, other interface).
Evidence options (vendor's choice — any ONE that proves compliance): (a) the full document / configuration; (b) a high-level or redacted version plus a signed attestation by an authorized officer that the control meets the referenced TB items; (c) independent certification or report (e.g., ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, cloud-provider compliance report, penetration-test summary letter); or (d) a view-only presentation (screen share or on site) recorded by the Validators as "sighted" with date, without keeping a copy. Source code, keys, credentials and internal network details are never required. Evidence is used only for this validation, under the Regional Validation Team's confidentiality undertaking (Instructions 4B).

Purpose: What matters is that patient details recorded once in the EMR are reused without manual re-encoding. Whether the eReferral function is built into the EMR or is a separate system is the vendor's design choice and is not penalised.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Review the architecture diagram.
2. Demonstration: register the Test Data patient in the EMR, then start a referral.
3. Fully integrated: every patient detail already in the EMR (name, birth date, sex, PhilSys number, PhilHealth ID, address, contact number) appears in the referral without the user re-typing, copy-pasting or re-uploading it — whether the eReferral function is built into the EMR or is a separate system connected to it.
4. Standalone - manual encoding: any of these details must be encoded manually.
5. Not Met: no diagram or no demonstration.

criteria.title: Product security and privacy design documented and stated against the Technical Baseline and NPC Circular 2023-06: (1) authentication & role-based access, (2) audit logging, (3) encryption in transit and at rest, (4) backup & recovery of data held only in the system (user accounts / credentials, audit trail, configuration), (5) privacy-by-design / privacy-by-default features — data minimisation, retention and secure disposal
criteria.evidence: Security design document, OR redacted summary + signed attestation, OR independent certification, OR view-only presentation
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit security and privacy design documentation covering the five topics. For each topic, state the mechanism used and confirm it meets or exceeds the Technical Baseline (Reference Guide, Ch. 3) (TB-01 to TB-11). Any product, platform or method is acceptable if it meets the baseline. If an equivalent control is used instead, attach a short justification with evidence (Instructions 4A).
Evidence options (vendor's choice — any ONE that proves compliance): (a) the full document / configuration; (b) a high-level or redacted version plus a signed attestation by an authorized officer that the control meets the referenced TB items; (c) independent certification or report (e.g., ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, cloud-provider compliance report, penetration-test summary letter); or (d) a view-only presentation (screen share or on site) recorded by the Validators as "sighted" with date, without keeping a copy. Source code, keys, credentials and internal network details are never required. Evidence is used only for this validation, under the Regional Validation Team's confidentiality undertaking (Instructions 4B).

Purpose: Describes the security features the system provides, in measurable terms. Referral data exchanged is kept on the Shared Health Record; the backup covers data that exists only in the system. Topic 5 also gives facilities (the personal information controllers) what they need for their own Privacy Impact Assessment under NPC Circular 2023-06 §5 and §7.
criteria.validator_guide:
Count the five topics. A topic is Met if compliance is shown by ANY accepted evidence option (full or redacted document with signed attestation, independent certification, or view-only presentation recorded as sighted) AND it is mapped to the referenced TB items (or an equivalent control was accepted by the Technical Lead). Record the evidence option used in Notes. Level 2D tests that the controls work.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.

sub_items.text: Encryption in transit and at rest, password storage (TB-01 to TB-04)
Backup & recovery of data held only in the system — user accounts / credentials, audit trail, configuration (TB-09)
Privacy-by-design / privacy-by-default — data minimisation, retention and secure disposal (TB-11; NPC Circular 2023-06 §7–9, §28–30)

criteria.title: Version/change management: release notes for the version under test and a committed timeline for updating to new IG versions
criteria.evidence: Release notes + update commitment
criteria.developer_guide:
Submit release notes for the version under test and a written timeline for adopting new PH Core / PHeReF IG versions.

Purpose: Updates to the draft IGs will be applied in a controlled, traceable way.
criteria.validator_guide: Check release notes for the version under test and the written update timeline.

sheets.title: Level 2A — TS0 Terminology & Registry Validation (GATE)
sheets.intro: Before submitting (TS1) or reading (TS2) an eReferral, every coded element must use the official terminology and every registry value or patient identifier must follow the official registry — the exact server, registry or API for each concept is named in the Terminology & Registry Sources (Reference Guide, Ch. 4) (SRC-01 to SRC-15). CRITICAL (must be 100%): the IG-required bindings (TS0-01, TS0-02), invalid-code handling (TS0-03), PSGC and NHFR (★ in TS0-06) and the PhilHealth / PhilSys identifiers (TS0-07) — TS1, TS2 and Level 3 cannot work without them. Other items (display text, code-system validity, NHWR, DSWD) carry normal weight but are not critical. How values are obtained (live look-up, scheduled sync or cached copy) is the vendor's choice. Test this part FIRST.

criteria.title: PH Core coded elements: values match the official PH Core / base FHIR value sets (required bindings — not locally invented)
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of each dropdown + server response ($expand / $validate-code)
criteria.developer_guide:
Use the PH Core / base FHIR value sets for each coded field listed (sex, contact point) — source SRC-05. Use the source named in the Terminology & Registry Sources (Reference Guide, Ch. 4) — for coded values, the DOH HIE terminology server (runtime look-up, scheduled sync or cached copy: vendor's choice).

Purpose: These bindings are REQUIRED in the IG; a wrong code makes the whole referral fail validation (TS1-T.02), so this is critical.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Check that the system's configured terminology endpoint is the DOH HIE terminology server (Terminology & Registry Sources — Reference Guide, Ch. 4).
2. Open each field / dropdown listed as a sub-item and compare the options with the value set on the server ($expand), or check the submitted code ($validate-code).
3. A sub-item is Met only if every option / submitted code belongs to the bound value set.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: Civil status — MaritalStatus value set (required binding in ERefPatient)
Accompanied by / next of kin relationship — RelatedPerson relationship type (required binding on Patient.contact.relationship)

criteria.title: PHeReF coded elements: values match the official PHeReF value sets (not locally invented)
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of each dropdown + server response ($expand / $validate-code)
criteria.developer_guide:
Use the PHeReF value sets for each coded field — sources SRC-01 to SRC-04 and SRC-09. Use the source named in the Terminology & Registry Sources (Reference Guide, Ch. 4) — for coded values, the DOH HIE terminology server (runtime look-up, scheduled sync or cached copy: vendor's choice).
Referral Category → ServiceRequest.category (Referral Category VS, SNOMED CT: 73770003 Emergency / 440655000 Outpatient — required). Priority → ServiceRequest.priority (EReferralPriority: routine / urgent / stat — required). Reason for Referral → ServiceRequest.reasonCode (Reason for Referral (Service Type) VS, SNOMED CT). Practitioner Role → PractitionerRole.code (Practitioner Role VS — required). Task status → Task.status (FHIR TaskStatus: requested, received, accepted, rejected, completed).

Purpose: TS1, TS2 and the Level 3 reports cannot work if these codes are wrong — all five are critical.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Check that the system's configured terminology endpoint is the DOH HIE terminology server (Terminology & Registry Sources — Reference Guide, Ch. 4).
2. Open each field / dropdown listed as a sub-item and compare the options with the value set on the server ($expand), or check the submitted code ($validate-code).
3. A sub-item is Met only if every option / submitted code belongs to the bound value set.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: Practitioner Role — PHeReF Practitioner Role VS (required binding)
Referral Category — PHeReF Referral Category VS, SNOMED CT Emergency / Outpatient (required binding)
Priority — EReferralPriority: routine / urgent / stat (required binding)
Reason for Referral (service type) — PHeReF Reason for Referral VS, SNOMED CT
Task status — FHIR TaskStatus (requested / received / accepted / rejected / completed)

criteria.title: Invalid codes are handled gracefully: the system prevents a code outside the bound value set, OR clearly shows the SHR's rejection to the user and lets them correct and resend (Connectathon Issue #25)
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of the block / error message + server-side evidence of the rejected and corrected submission
criteria.developer_guide:
Either (a) validate coded fields before saving / sending (e.g., pick-lists built from the value set, $validate-code) so an out-of-value-set code cannot be entered, or (b) when the SHR rejects the referral, show the user a clear error naming the field and allow correction and resend. Which approach is used is the vendor's choice.

Purpose: Wrong codes never silently enter the referral or the dashboards, and users are never left with a failed referral they cannot see.
criteria.validator_guide:
Validator (server-side) attempts to submit one code outside the value set (e.g., for Reason for Referral).
Met if EITHER the EMR blocks / flags it before sending, OR the EMR displays the SHR's rejection in understandable terms and the user can correct and resend successfully.
Not Met if the error is not shown to the user, or the code is accepted.

criteria.title: Codes are displayed with their official display text (no locally renamed labels)
criteria.evidence: Screenshots side-by-side
criteria.developer_guide:
Display the official display text from the terminology server; do not rename code labels locally. A local translation may be shown in addition to, not instead of, the official text.

Purpose: Everyone sees the same meaning for the same code.
criteria.validator_guide:
Compare displayed labels for 3 value sets against the terminology server display. Count matching value sets.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: Reason for Referral — official display text

criteria.title: International code systems used where the PH Core / PHeReF IG binds them are valid codes on the DOH terminology server: SNOMED CT, LOINC and ICD-10
criteria.evidence: $validate-code / $validate output
criteria.developer_guide:
Where the IG binds a field to SNOMED CT (practitioner role, referral category, reason for referral) or LOINC (vital-sign Observation codes), or ICD-10 (working impression, where bound), send codes that exist in the edition loaded on the DOH terminology server, with the correct system URI.

Purpose: Codes are valid and comparable across facilities.
criteria.validator_guide:
Validator (server-side) runs CodeSystem/$validate-code on the DOH terminology server (or $validate on the submitted bundle) for every SNOMED CT, LOINC and ICD-10 code in the Test Data referral. A sub-item is Met only if every code of that system is valid.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: SNOMED CT — codes valid; system = http://snomed.info/sct
LOINC — vital-sign codes valid; system = http://loinc.org
ICD-10 — working-impression codes valid; system = http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10 (N/A if not bound)

criteria.title: Geographic, facility and health-worker values come from the official national registries and match them: PSGC, NHFR, NHWR
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of each field + registry / server response
criteria.developer_guide:
Take PSGC codes from the PSA PSGC release announced by the DOH (SRC-10), facility codes from the NHFR (SRC-11) and practitioner identifiers from the NHWR / PRC (SRC-12). How the registry is accessed (API, scheduled sync or official download) is the vendor's choice; the release must match the DOH server.

Purpose: PSGC and NHFR are critical — the receiving facility finds its referrals by NHFR code (TS2-01) and the Level 3 reports group by facility and municipality.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Open each field listed as a sub-item and compare the values with the source named in the Terminology & Registry Sources (Reference Guide, Ch. 4).
2. Server-side check: confirm the submitted codes exist in that registry / the DOH terminology server.
3. For NHFR (TS0-06.2): try to type a facility that is not in the NHFR — the system must only allow selecting NHFR facilities (absorbs Rev 6 L4-09).
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: PSGC code — Philippine Standard Geographic Code (PSA)
NHFR code — National Health Facility Registry; facilities selected only from the NHFR, not free-typed (absorbs Rev 6 L4-09)
NHWR — health worker identifier / licence no. (National Health Workforce Registry)

criteria.title: Patient identifiers — PhilHealth ID and PhilSys number — are captured, validated and sent with the official PH Core identifier system, so that every patient record is linked to them (CRITICAL)
criteria.evidence: SHR Patient resource + error screenshot for the malformed value
criteria.developer_guide:
For every patient: (1) provide fields for the PhilHealth ID and the PhilSys number; (2) validate the format per the PH Core IG and reject malformed values; (3) send each as Patient.identifier with the PH Core identifier system (PHCorePhilHealthID / PHCorePhilSysID); (4) where a verification service is made available for the sandbox — e.g., the PhilSys Verifier through the DSWD dxCLOUD API under an agreement with DSWD (SRC-14), or a PhilHealth service (SRC-13) — use it. If a patient genuinely has no number yet, the record may be saved with the reason recorded (e.g., "not yet registered") so it can be linked later — the system must never invent or default a number. How validation is implemented is the vendor's choice.

Purpose: Patients are expected to be linked to their PhilHealth and PhilSys numbers across the network; these identifiers are the keys for matching records and avoiding duplicates (L4-08).
criteria.validator_guide:
For EACH identifier (sub-item):
1. Enter the Test Data value and submit; Validator (server-side) retrieves the Patient and confirms identifier.system and value match PH Core and the Test Data.
2. Enter one malformed value (e.g., wrong number of digits, or letters); the system must reject it.
3. If a verification service is available on the sandbox, confirm the system used it.
Met only if all applicable steps pass. CRITICAL — both sub-items must be Met.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.

sub_items.text: PhilHealth ID (PhilHealth) — official identifier system, format validated, malformed value rejected
PhilSys number (PSA) — official identifier system, format validated, malformed value rejected

criteria.title: OPTIONAL — DSWD household / beneficiary identifier (Household No. or UBD ID) can be recorded and, where DSWD grants API access, looked up through the DSWD dxCLOUD API (SRC-15)
criteria.evidence: Screenshot (optional)
criteria.developer_guide: Provide a field for the DSWD household / beneficiary identifier. Where DSWD has granted API access and a data sharing agreement is in place, the system may look it up or verify it through the DSWD dxCLOUD API (https://dxcloud.dswd.gov.ph/api/documentation — e.g., /api/person/getUBID, /api/person/verifyPantawid). Optional and not scored until the TDG defines the PH Core / PHeReF mapping.
criteria.validator_guide: Record whether the field exists and, if DSWD API access was granted, whether a look-up works (for information only).

sheets.title: Level 2B — TS1 eReferral Submission by Referring Facility
sheets.intro: The referring facility submits the Test Data referral to the Shared Health Record (SHR). Every item is verified ON THE SERVER using any one form of server-side evidence: an Interoperability Layer log (e.g., OpenHIM), an Inferno / FHIR validator report, or the raw request / response payload from the developer. Fields are grouped by FHIR resource — open the resource once and tick its fields. ★ marks critical sub-items. How the data is sent (HTTP verbs, bundle style) is the vendor's choice.

criteria.title: Referring (initiating) facility details are submitted correctly
criteria.evidence: Server-side evidence (IOL log, Inferno / validator report, or raw payload) + resource ID
criteria.developer_guide:
Capture the fields below in the EMR and send them in the Organization (referring facility) per the PHeReF / PH Core profile. Any create / update method is accepted (transaction Bundle recommended; conditional create / update allowed) — HTTP verbs are not prescribed. What is tested is that the values reach the SHR in the profiled resource and can be retrieved.
FHIR elements: Organization.name; Organization.identifier (NHFR; HCPN); Organization.address (PSGC-coded); Organization.telecom
Source: SRC-10, SRC-11, SRC-05 (Terminology & Registry Sources — Reference Guide, Ch. 4)

Purpose: The receiving facility knows exactly where the patient comes from.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Enter the Test Data values for this group (Test Data Section A) in the referring EMR and submit the referral.
2. Open the Organization in the server-side evidence and compare each sub-item with the Test Data value.
3. Record the resource ID / log reference in Notes.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

criteria.title: Receiving facility details are submitted correctly
criteria.evidence: Server-side evidence (IOL log, Inferno / validator report, or raw payload) + resource ID
criteria.developer_guide:
Capture the fields below in the EMR and send them in the Organization (receiving facility) per the PHeReF / PH Core profile. Any create / update method is accepted (transaction Bundle recommended; conditional create / update allowed) — HTTP verbs are not prescribed. What is tested is that the values reach the SHR in the profiled resource and can be retrieved.
FHIR elements: Organization.name; Organization.identifier (NHFR); Organization.address — referenced from ServiceRequest.performer / Task.owner
Source: SRC-10, SRC-11 (Terminology & Registry Sources — Reference Guide, Ch. 4)

Purpose: The referral is addressed to the right facility so it appears in that facility's incoming list.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Enter the Test Data values for this group (Test Data Section A) in the referring EMR and submit the referral.
2. Open the Organization in the server-side evidence and compare each sub-item with the Test Data value.
3. Record the resource ID / log reference in Notes.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

criteria.title: Referring practitioner (and care navigator, if assigned) is submitted correctly and linked as the requester
criteria.evidence: Server-side evidence (IOL log, Inferno / validator report, or raw payload) + resource ID
criteria.developer_guide:
Capture the fields below in the EMR and send them in the PractitionerRole + Practitioner (referring facility) per the PHeReF / PH Core profile. Any create / update method is accepted (transaction Bundle recommended; conditional create / update allowed) — HTTP verbs are not prescribed. What is tested is that the values reach the SHR in the profiled resource and can be retrieved.
FHIR elements: Practitioner.name; PractitionerRole.code (Practitioner Role VS); referenced by ServiceRequest.requester and Task.requester. A care navigator at the referring facility, where assigned, is a separate PractitionerRole (role code from the Practitioner Role VS).
Source: SRC-01, SRC-12 (Terminology & Registry Sources — Reference Guide, Ch. 4)

Purpose: The receiving facility knows who is accountable for the referral and whom to call back.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Enter the Test Data values for this group (Test Data Section A) in the referring EMR and submit the referral.
2. Open the PractitionerRole + Practitioner in the server-side evidence and compare each sub-item with the Test Data value.
3. Record the resource ID / log reference in Notes.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Care navigator at the referring facility, if assigned — separate PractitionerRole (N/A if the facility does not assign one)
Referring practitioner is the requester of the ServiceRequest and the Task (not the receiving practitioner)

criteria.title: Patient demographics and identifiers are submitted correctly
criteria.evidence: Server-side evidence (IOL log, Inferno / validator report, or raw payload) + resource ID
criteria.developer_guide:
Capture the fields below in the EMR and send them in the Patient (ERefPatient / PH Core Patient) per the PHeReF / PH Core profile. Any create / update method is accepted (transaction Bundle recommended; conditional create / update allowed) — HTTP verbs are not prescribed. What is tested is that the values reach the SHR in the profiled resource and can be retrieved.
FHIR elements: Patient.name; Patient.identifier (PH Core PhilSys and PhilHealth slices); Patient.birthDate; Patient.gender; Patient.maritalStatus; Patient.address (PSGC-coded); Patient.telecom; PWD Disability Registration extension. Age is NOT sent — the receiving system computes it from birthDate (checked in TS2-04).
Source: SRC-05, SRC-10, SRC-13, SRC-14 (Terminology & Registry Sources — Reference Guide, Ch. 4)

Purpose: The patient is identified unambiguously across facilities.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Enter the Test Data values for this group (Test Data Section A) in the referring EMR and submit the referral.
2. Open the Patient in the server-side evidence and compare each sub-item with the Test Data value.

Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Care navigator at the receiving facility — Task.owner (N/A if the facility does not assign one)
Referring and receiving practitioners are stored and displayed as separate people — not merged or overwritten

criteria.title: Receiving facility response updates the referral Task on the SHR (received → accepted / rejected → completed)
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + server-side evidence of each Task update
criteria.developer_guide:
Update the Task on the SHR when the receiving facility acts: received, then accepted or rejected (with reason in Task.statusReason), then completed (Task.executionPeriod.end). Receiving responses follow the eReferral Receiving Facility Response VS. Any update method is accepted.

Purpose: Both facilities and the dashboards see the true status of every referral.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. In the receiving EMR, mark the Test Data referral Received, then Accepted, then Completed.
2. Use a second test referral to Reject with a reason.
3. Confirm each new status on the SHR with the server-side evidence. (Status timestamps are checked in TS2-13.)
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Rejected with reason — Task.status = rejected + statusReason (second test referral)

criteria.title: Status changes made by the receiving facility are shown at the referring facility
criteria.evidence: Screenshot at referring EMR + server-side evidence
criteria.developer_guide:
Read the updated Task from the SHR (polling, subscription or IOL notification — vendor's choice) and show the current status to the referring facility.

Purpose: The referring facility knows whether the patient is expected.
criteria.validator_guide:
Change the status at the receiving EMR (TS2-11); Met if the referring EMR shows the new status, including a rejection and its reason.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

criteria.title: Every status change of the referral is time-stamped and kept: requested, received, accepted / rejected, completed (moved from L4-06; Connectathon Issue #26)
criteria.evidence: Task history / Provenance from the SHR
criteria.developer_guide:
Record the date/time of each Task status change so the history can be read back (Task history / versions, Provenance, or Task.lastModified per update — vendor's choice; ERefTask marks authoredOn and lastModified as Must Support). Earlier timestamps must not be overwritten.

Purpose: Needed for audit and for turnaround time (IND-08).
criteria.validator_guide:
Validator (server-side) reads the Task history (_history) or the linked Provenance on the SHR after TS2-11. Count the 4 status changes that have a date/time that matches when they were made.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Received — date/time recorded and kept (absorbs Rev 6 TS2-11.5)
Accepted / rejected — date/time recorded and kept

sheets.title: Level 2D — Security, Reliability & Exception Handling
sheets.intro: Baseline technical safeguards required before live patient data is exchanged. Each criterion states the OUTCOME tested; the minimum measurable specification is given in the Technical Baseline (Reference Guide, Ch. 3) (TB-01 to TB-14). Any product, platform or method that meets or exceeds the baseline is acceptable. Outcomes are tested by using the system (black-box); where documents are needed, vendors may choose any evidence option in Instructions 4B — internals and trade secrets are never required. DISCLAIMER: this is SECURITY CONFORMANCE TESTING of defined controls. Passing it is NOT equivalent to passing a vulnerability assessment and penetration test (VAPT) or a full cybersecurity assessment (TEC-14 only checks that an independent assessment exists). EXCEPTION HANDLING (TS3-01 to TS3-09): the EMR must not show a failed exchange as successful, must explain the error, allow correction, and leave exactly one correct referral on the SHR — inputs and expected results are in Test Data Section D (TD-D##).

criteria.title: All data exchange is encrypted in transit and meets Technical Baseline TB-01 and TB-02 (TLS 1.2 or higher, strong cipher suites, valid certificate)
criteria.evidence: Endpoint list + TLS scan report per endpoint
criteria.developer_guide:
Encrypt every endpoint used for the eReferral (EMR ↔ SHR, terminology server, user access) with TLS 1.2 or higher and a valid certificate; disable plain HTTP or redirect it to HTTPS; disable SSL, TLS 1.0/1.1 and weak cipher suites (TB-01, TB-02). Any web server, gateway, proxy or cloud service may be used.

Purpose: Patient data cannot be read or changed while travelling over the network.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. List every endpoint used.
2. Validator (server-side) scans each endpoint with a TLS testing tool (e.g., testssl.sh, nmap ssl-enum-ciphers or an online TLS checker).
3. Met only if EVERY endpoint uses https://, negotiates TLS 1.2 or 1.3 only, offers no cipher suite listed as not acceptable in TB-02, and has a valid, unexpired certificate matching the host name.

criteria.title: Each user has a unique account; no shared logins
criteria.evidence: User account list
criteria.developer_guide:
Require one account per user; no generic or shared accounts. Protect accounts per TB-05 (minimum password length, failed-attempt lock-out or throttling, no default passwords). Any identity method is acceptable (local accounts, LDAP / Active Directory, single sign-on, OpenID Connect).

Purpose: Every action can be traced to a person.
criteria.validator_guide: Check that the system requires a unique account per user and that no generic/shared accounts are used for test referrals. Then try (a) a password shorter than the TB-05 minimum and (b) repeated failed log-ins. Met only if all three behave as TB-05 requires.

criteria.title: Role-based access works: (1) referring clinician, (2) receiving clinician, (3) administrator, (4) report/dashboard viewer see only what their role allows
criteria.evidence: Screenshots per role
criteria.developer_guide:
Implement role-based access for referring clinician, receiving clinician, administrator and report viewer.

Purpose: Staff only see the data they need.
criteria.validator_guide:
Log in with each of the 4 roles and try one action outside the role. Count roles that behave correctly.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.

sub_items.text: Report / dashboard viewer role restricted correctly

criteria.title: Audit trail records who did what and when
criteria.evidence: Audit log extract
criteria.developer_guide:
Log user, date/time and action for create, view, edit, send, receive, accept, decline, print, export and log-in events, with the fields required by TB-08. The storage format (database table, log file, FHIR AuditEvent, SIEM) is the vendor's choice.

Purpose: Needed for accountability and privacy compliance.
criteria.validator_guide:
Perform the 10 actions listed in the Notes (create, view, edit, send, receive, accept, decline, print, export, log-in). Count the actions found in the audit log with user and time.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.

criteria.title: Automatic log-out after inactivity
criteria.evidence: Screenshot / configuration
criteria.developer_guide:
Log the user out, or lock the session and require re-authentication, after an idle period the facility can configure; the default must not exceed the TB-06 value.

Purpose: Unattended screens do not expose patient data.
criteria.validator_guide: Check the configured idle period (default per TB-06), then leave a session idle for that time. Met if the user is logged out or the session is locked and requires re-authentication.

criteria.title: Backup and restore of data held only in the system (user accounts / credentials, roles, audit trail, configuration)
criteria.evidence: Restore demonstration, OR restore-test record, OR provider backup report + signed attestation
criteria.developer_guide:
Provide backup and restore of data held only in the system — user accounts / credentials, roles, audit trail and configuration — meeting TB-09 (automated, encrypted, stored separately). The backup tool and location are the vendor's choice.
Evidence options (vendor's choice — any ONE that proves compliance): (a) the full document / configuration; (b) a high-level or redacted version plus a signed attestation by an authorized officer that the control meets the referenced TB items; (c) independent certification or report (e.g., ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, cloud-provider compliance report, penetration-test summary letter); or (d) a view-only presentation (screen share or on site) recorded by the Validators as "sighted" with date, without keeping a copy. Source code, keys, credentials and internal network details are never required. Evidence is used only for this validation, under the Regional Validation Team's confidentiality undertaking (Instructions 4B).

Purpose: Data that exists only in the system — not on the Shared Health Record — can be recovered after a failure.

criteria.title: Data held by the system is encrypted at rest (TB-03) and user passwords are stored only as salted adaptive hashes (TB-04)
criteria.evidence: Any accepted evidence option (view-only demo, masked screenshots, certification + signed attestation)
criteria.developer_guide:
Encrypt personal and health data held by the system — database, stored files/attachments and backups — with AES-128 or stronger, keeping keys separate from the data (TB-03). Store passwords only as salted hashes using Argon2id, bcrypt, scrypt or PBKDF2 (TB-04). Any encryption layer is acceptable (full-disk/volume, database, file or field level).
Evidence options (vendor's choice — any ONE that proves compliance): (a) the full document / configuration; (b) a high-level or redacted version plus a signed attestation by an authorized officer that the control meets the referenced TB items; (c) independent certification or report (e.g., ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, cloud-provider compliance report, penetration-test summary letter); or (d) a view-only presentation (screen share or on site) recorded by the Validators as "sighted" with date, without keeping a copy. Source code, keys, credentials and internal network details are never required. Evidence is used only for this validation, under the Regional Validation Team's confidentiality undertaking (Instructions 4B).

Purpose: A stolen disk, database copy or backup does not expose patient data or passwords.

criteria.title: Access boundaries hold: failed log-ins are handled safely, users cannot see or act on another facility's referrals, and users cannot raise their own privileges
criteria.evidence: Screenshots / HTTP responses per step (black-box)
criteria.developer_guide:
Enforce authorisation on the SERVER side for every screen and API call: by role (TEC-03) and by facility (a user acts only for the facility/ies assigned). Reject guessed or changed record IDs that belong to another facility. Use generic log-in error messages and lock-out / throttling per TB-05.

Purpose: Prevents the most common real-world breaches — staff or outsiders reading records they are not entitled to.
criteria.validator_guide:
Use two test accounts: User A (referring clinician, Facility A) and User B (receiving clinician, Facility B), plus TD-D18 to TD-D21.
1. Enter a wrong password for a valid user and for a non-existent user: messages must be identical; after the TB-05 limit the account is locked or throttled.
2. As User A, try to open a referral addressed only to Facility C (list, search, direct link).
3. Change the referral / patient ID in the URL or API call to one belonging to Facility C.
4. As a non-administrator, open an administrator page by direct URL / API and try to change your own role.
5. Call the EMR's API without a valid session / token.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.

sub_items.text: Failed log-in: generic message (no user enumeration) and lock-out / throttling per TB-05 (TD-D18)
Cross-facility access blocked — referrals of another facility cannot be listed, searched or opened (TD-D19)
Direct object reference blocked — changing an ID in the URL / API does not reveal another facility's data (TD-D20)
No privilege escalation — admin functions unreachable by direct URL / API; users cannot change their own role (TD-D21)
Requests without a valid session / token are refused (HTTP 401 / 403 or redirect to log-in)

criteria.title: Sessions and accounts end when they should: log-out invalidates the session, expired sessions / tokens are refused, and revoked accounts lose access
criteria.evidence: Screenshots / HTTP responses + time of each step
criteria.developer_guide:
Invalidate the session on the server at log-out; refuse expired sessions and tokens; when an administrator deactivates an account, block new log-ins immediately and end its active sessions within the TB-12 limit.

Purpose: Departed staff and stolen sessions cannot keep accessing patient data.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Log in, copy the session (or note the page), log out, then press Back / replay the request: access must be refused.
2. Wait past the idle / token expiry (TB-06 / TB-12) and repeat an action: re-authentication is required.
3. Administrator deactivates a logged-in test user: the user cannot log in again, and the open session ends within the TB-12 limit.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.

sub_items.text: Session invalid after log-out (Back / replayed request refused)
Expired session / token refused; re-authentication required
Deactivated account: new log-in blocked immediately; active session ended within the TB-12 limit

criteria.title: Error messages, client-side code and logs do not expose secrets, system internals or patient data beyond what the user may see
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + log sample or signed attestation
criteria.developer_guide:
Show users generic error messages (no stack traces, SQL, file paths or server versions); keep credentials, tokens and API keys out of browser / mobile code, URLs and browser storage (TB-07); keep full identifiers and clinical content out of application logs except where required by TB-08 audit (TB-13).

Purpose: Error screens and logs are a frequent source of data leaks.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Trigger errors (TD-D03, a non-existent page, a broken request) and read the messages.
2. Open the browser developer tools (or inspect the mobile app traffic) and look for secrets in source, URLs, local / session storage.
3. Review a sample application log from the test session, OR accept a signed attestation with a redacted sample (Instructions 4B).
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.

sub_items.text: Error messages show no stack trace, SQL, paths, versions or unauthorised patient data
No credentials / tokens / API keys in client code, URLs or browser storage
Application logs exclude secrets and unnecessary personal data (TB-13)

criteria.title: The audit log cannot be altered through the application and records security events
criteria.evidence: Audit log extract + screenshots
criteria.developer_guide:
Make audit entries append-only for every application role, including administrators; log failed log-ins, role / permission changes and account deactivation; restrict viewing / export of the audit log to an authorised role (TB-08).

Purpose: An audit trail that can be edited proves nothing.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. As an ordinary user and as an administrator, try to edit or delete an audit entry through the application.
2. Check that the failed log-ins (TEC-09.1), the role change attempt (TEC-09.4) and the deactivation (TEC-10.3) appear in the log.
3. Try to open the audit log with a non-authorised role.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.

sub_items.text: Audit entries cannot be edited or deleted through the application (any role)
Role / permission changes and account deactivation are logged
Audit log viewing / export restricted to an authorised role

criteria.title: Outgoing connections verify server certificates, and any API the EMR exposes is protected against abuse
criteria.evidence: Connection error screenshot / log + throttling response or documented control
criteria.developer_guide:
Validate the certificate of the SHR / terminology server on every connection (no 'trust all certificates' setting). If the EMR exposes its own API to the internet, apply rate limiting or equivalent abuse controls.

Purpose: Prevents interception (man-in-the-middle) and denial-of-service by request flooding.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D22: the DOH provides a sandbox endpoint with an invalid / expired / untrusted certificate; point the EMR to it. Met if the EMR refuses to connect (N/A with reason if the DOH has not provisioned the endpoint).
2. If the EMR exposes an internet-facing API: send repeated requests (within the agreed test limit) and confirm throttling or a documented control. N/A if no API is exposed.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.

sub_items.text: Connection refused to an endpoint with an invalid / untrusted certificate (TD-D22)
Rate limiting / abuse control on any internet-facing API exposed by the EMR (N/A if none)

criteria.title: An independent vulnerability assessment (VAPT or authenticated scan) of the version under test exists, with no unresolved critical / high findings
criteria.evidence: VAPT / scan executive summary + signed attestation (or full report, view-only)
criteria.developer_guide:
Provide evidence of a vulnerability assessment and penetration test or an authenticated vulnerability scan of the version under test (or the same major version) done within the last 12 months by an independent party or a separate security team (TB-14), with critical / high findings fixed or covered by a remediation plan accepted by the Technical Lead. Evidence options per Instructions 4B (e.g., executive summary + signed attestation).

Purpose: Black-box conformance testing cannot replace a security assessment; this checks one was done.
criteria.validator_guide: Check the date, scope (product + version), assessor independence and the status of critical / high findings. Met only if all four are acceptable. This criterion does NOT make this validation a security assessment (see disclaimer above).

criteria.title: A referral missing an element the IG makes mandatory is not shown as sent, the reason is shown to the user, and the corrected referral is accepted
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of the block / error + server-side evidence of the rejected and the accepted submission
criteria.developer_guide:
Prevent sending, OR handle the SHR rejection (HTTP 4xx with OperationOutcome) of a referral that lacks an element with minimum cardinality ≥ 1 in the PHeReF / PH Core profiles (see FHIR Traceability (Reference Guide, Ch. 5), column 'Cardinality'). Show the user which item is missing, keep the referral as not sent, and allow correction and resend.

Purpose: A referral that the SHR refused must never look 'sent' to the referring clinician.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Use TD-D01 (patient birth date left blank) and TD-D02 (receiving facility not selected).
2. For each sub-item: try to submit. Met if EITHER the EMR blocks it before sending with a clear message, OR the SHR rejects it and the EMR shows the rejection in understandable terms and keeps the referral as NOT sent.
3. Correct the value and resend; confirm on the SHR that exactly one accepted referral exists.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Missing Patient.birthDate (1..1) — blocked or rejection shown; referral not marked sent (TD-D01)
Missing receiving facility (ServiceRequest.performer) — blocked or rejection shown (TD-D02)
After correction, the referral is accepted and exactly one ServiceRequest / Task exists on the SHR

criteria.title: Malformed values (wrong data type or format) are prevented or the SHR rejection is handled without data loss
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + server-side evidence (where submitted)
criteria.developer_guide:
Validate data types and formats before sending (dates in ISO 8601, numeric vital signs with UCUM units, identifier formats per PH Core), OR handle the SHR rejection clearly. Entered data must not be lost when an error occurs.

Purpose: Bad formats are caught early and do not reach other facilities.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Use TD-D03 (impossible date, e.g., 2026-02-30), TD-D04 (non-numeric heart rate) and TD-D05 (birth date in the future).
2. Met per sub-item if the system blocks the value OR shows the SHR rejection clearly, and the rest of the entered referral is kept for correction.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Impossible date (TD-D03) — prevented or rejection handled
Non-numeric vital-sign value (TD-D04) — prevented or rejection handled
Birth date in the future (TD-D05) — prevented or rejection handled

criteria.title: References to a facility, practitioner or patient that does not exist are prevented or the rejection is handled
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + server-side evidence
criteria.developer_guide:
Resolve every reference before sending — facilities from the NHFR (TS0-06), practitioners from the registered list — OR handle the SHR rejection of an unresolvable reference clearly.

Purpose: A referral cannot be addressed to a facility that does not exist.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. Use TD-D06 (NHFR code not in the registry) and TD-D07 (practitioner not registered in the sandbox).
2. Met per sub-item if the system blocks it OR shows the SHR rejection clearly and keeps the referral as not sent.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Unknown receiving facility NHFR code (TD-D06) — prevented or handled
Unregistered practitioner as requester (TD-D07) — prevented or handled

criteria.title: Submitting the same referral twice (double click, resend after timeout, re-opened draft) leaves only ONE referral on the SHR
criteria.evidence: SHR search result (count of ServiceRequest / Task) + server-side evidence
criteria.developer_guide:
Make sending idempotent — e.g., disable the Send action while waiting, give each referral a business identifier and use conditional create (If-None-Exist) or a transaction Bundle with conditional entries, or check the SHR before resending. The method is the vendor's choice.

Purpose: Duplicate referrals distort Level 3 counts and make the receiving facility prepare twice.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D08: click Send twice quickly. 2. TD-D09: after a send, use the system's own resend / retry function for the same referral.
3. Validator (server-side) searches the SHR (ServiceRequest by patient and authored date, or by business identifier).
Met per sub-item only if exactly ONE ServiceRequest and ONE Task exist for that referral.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Double Send (TD-D08) — exactly one ServiceRequest and one Task on the SHR
Resend / retry of an already accepted referral (TD-D09) — no second referral created

criteria.title: Connection loss during or before sending: no data is lost, the referral is sent (automatically or by documented fallback) after recovery, and exactly one copy arrives
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + server-side evidence + fallback record (if manual)
criteria.developer_guide:
Queue referrals made during connection loss and resend automatically, OR provide a documented manual fallback (user manual L1-02.5). After recovery the referral must arrive once, with the original date/time referred (absorbs Rev 6 TEC-06).

Purpose: Referrals continue during outages without loss or duplication.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D10: disconnect the network, create and send a referral; reconnect.
2. TD-D11: interrupt the connection while a send is in progress (e.g., disable the network adapter immediately after Send).
3. Met per sub-item if, after recovery, exactly one copy is on the SHR with the original authoredOn, and the user was told the status (queued / failed / sent).
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Offline creation (TD-D10) — queued or documented fallback followed; user sees status
Interruption mid-send (TD-D11) — no loss; exactly one copy after recovery
Original date/time referred kept after delayed sending (ServiceRequest.authoredOn)

criteria.title: If one part of the referral fails, no half-saved referral is left on the SHR and the EMR does not report success
criteria.evidence: Server-side evidence of the failed attempt + SHR search showing no orphan resources
criteria.developer_guide:
Send the referral so that it succeeds or fails as a whole — e.g., a FHIR transaction Bundle (all-or-nothing) as in the IG example (ExampleERefSubmissionBundle), or compensating clean-up when resources are sent one by one. Report failure to the user.

Purpose: A ServiceRequest without its Task, Patient or clinical data is unusable for the receiving facility.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D12: include one invalid resource in the referral (e.g., an Observation with a code outside LOINC, prepared with the developer).
2. Submit. Validator (server-side) checks the SHR.
Met per sub-item if no ServiceRequest / Task / partial resources from that attempt remain, and the EMR shows the failure.
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically. ★ = critical sub-item: if it is Not Met (or N/A) the criterion counts as a critical failure.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: No orphan or half-saved resources from the failed attempt on the SHR
EMR does not show the referral as sent; the user can correct and resend

criteria.title: When the terminology server or a registry (NHFR / PSGC) is unavailable, the EMR degrades gracefully and never sends invented codes
criteria.evidence: Screenshots + server-side evidence of codes sent
criteria.developer_guide:
When a look-up service is unreachable, use a validated cached copy (scheduled sync — see Terminology & Registry Sources, Reference Guide Ch. 4) OR block the coded field with a clear message. Never substitute free text or locally invented codes for a bound element.

Purpose: An outage of a national service must not corrupt the data exchanged.
criteria.validator_guide:
1. TD-D13: the DOH makes the terminology server unreachable for the test account (or the developer points the EMR to a dead endpoint).
2. TD-D14: same for the NHFR / facility list.
3. Met per sub-item if the EMR uses a valid cached value set OR blocks with a clear message, and any code sent is valid (TS0 check on the SHR).
Mark each sub-item (↳) below; Achieved is counted automatically.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

sub_items.text: Terminology server unavailable (TD-D13) — cached valid codes or clear block; no invented codes
Facility registry unavailable (TD-D14) — cached NHFR list or clear block; no free-typed facility

criteria.title: A rejected or expired system credential (EMR ↔ SHR) is reported clearly, nothing is silently dropped, and no secret appears in the message
criteria.evidence: Screenshot of the message + server-side evidence (401 / 403, then success after restore)
criteria.developer_guide:
Detect HTTP 401 / 403 from the SHR, tell the user (or administrator) that the connection credential failed, keep the referral as not sent / queued, and never display tokens, passwords or keys in messages or logs (TB-07, TB-13).

Purpose: Expired credentials are a common cause of silent referral loss.
criteria.validator_guide:
TD-D15: the DOH revokes or expires the system credential of the test EMR (or the developer configures an invalid one). Send a referral.
Met only if the user sees an understandable failure, the referral remains not sent / queued, it is sent after the credential is restored, and no secret is shown.
Server-side evidence — any ONE of: (a) Interoperability Layer transaction log (e.g., OpenHIM), (b) Inferno / official FHIR validator report, or (c) the raw FHIR request / response payload provided by the developer and captured during the session.

criteria.title: Receiving side: retrieval during an SHR outage is handled, nothing is missed after recovery, and the same referral is never listed twice
criteria.evidence: Screenshots of incoming list + server-side evidence

sheets.title: Level 4 — Advanced Interoperability
sheets.intro: Advanced interoperability. Rev 7 separates two tracks: CORE-TRACK items are fundamental interoperability requirements that will MIGRATE to Level 2 (minimum conformance) as soon as the PHeReF IG models them (back-referral and the multi-tier referral chain are not yet modelled in IG v0.1.0); MATURITY items are capability targets that remain optional. Moved to Level 2 in Rev 7: status timestamps (L4-06 → TS2-13), patient de-duplication (L4-08 → TS1-16) and NHFR-sourced facility data (L4-09 → TS0-06.2). The track is shown in the Section column.

retired.reason: Downtime handling now tested with retry / duplication checks in the TS3 exception scenarios of Level 2D.
Status timestamps are fundamental — now critical in Level 2.
Patient de-duplication is fundamental — now critical in Level 2.
NHFR-sourced facility data checked with the NHFR critical sub-item.
Received date/time now checked in the status-history criterion.
Identifier format validation (Connectathon Issue #5) moved to TS0-07 as a critical item. Number not reused.
Official conformance suite (Inferno) — removed until an official PHeReF test kit exists.
SMART on FHIR launch — removed; maturity target outside current scope.
